title: Rollout safety and telemetry-driven rollback playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a standardized, cross-team procedure for safe rollouts of model or runtime changes and for automated/manual rollback triggered by telemetry. It bridges API, infra, model-serving, observability, and performance standards so rollouts are predictable, auditable, and reversible without sacrificing customer SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to any change that impacts inference behavior: model weights, tokenizer, model config, quantization profile, runtime flags, compilation artifacts, or routing rules.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific change controls for Dedicated/Private deployments; instead this is the recommended blueprint for Redwood-hosted and internal staging environments.

Principles:
- Safety-first: prefer smaller, observable steps with automatic guardrails rather than large, fast rollouts.
- Signal-driven: telemetry defines progress and rollback. Predefined SLI/SLO-driven thresholds are mandatory for automated actions.
- Contract verification: API and output-schema compatibility checks must pass before traffic shift.
- Ownership and auditability: each rollout has an owner, a single rollback authority on-call, and an immutable audit trail.

Preconditions (gates before any rollout begins):
1) Contract tests green: schema/field-level checks and structured response contract tests run successfully. Example command:
   redwoodctl contract-verify --model-id $MODEL --path ./contracts/$MODEL-contract.yaml
2) Performance budget check: synthetic load test results within acceptable delta vs baseline per the PRD: P95 latency delta < 15% and tail (P99) degradation < 25%.
3) Quality baseline: evaluation harness (eval-harness) run shows no negative delta > 1.5% on primary quality metric (accuracy/ROUGE/F1 depending on workload).
4) Telemetry pipeline subscribed: canary telemetry stream length >= 10 minutes ingestion and baseline stable.
5) Owner and rollback authority assigned in rollout metadata.

Rollout sequence (recommended order):
1) Preflight (0%): run contract-verify, smoke tests, artifact provenance checks, and deployment dry-run.
2) Canary (1% traffic for 30–60 minutes): verify immediate errors, basic SLIs, and quality sampling.
3) Early expansion (5% for 30 minutes): check cost, latency, and user-facing error rates.
4) Mid expansion (25% for 1 hour): run sampling evals across representative workloads; check downstream services.
5) Ramp (75% for 2+ hours): monitor long-tail metrics and production regressions.
6) Full (100%): final validation and mark rollout complete.

Timing and guardrails are configurable per-product but must be declared in rollout metadata. Example YAML snippet for rollout policy:

rollout_policy: |
  id: rlb-2026-029
  owner: @priya.nair
  canary: {percent: 1, min_duration: 30m}
  stages:
    - {percent: 5, min_duration: 30m}
    - {percent: 25, min_duration: 60m}
    - {percent: 75, min_duration: 120m}
  final: {percent: 100}
  automatic_rollback: true

Telemetry and SLI mapping (table):
| SLI name | Signal source | Alert/rollback threshold | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| request_error_rate | edge-proxy.metrics.error_rate | > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 15m | High priority; immediate rollback if for canary |
| latency_p95 | runtime.metrics.latency_p95 | > 15% increase sustained 30m | Consider staged rollback / throttling first |
| latency_p99 | runtime.metrics.latency_p99 | > 30% increase sustained 15m | Tail latency spikes often indicate kernel fallback |
| quality_regression | eval.pipeline.quality_delta | > 1.5% negative delta on primary metric | Stop rollout; manual review required |
| cost_per_token | billing.derive.cost_per_token | > 40% increase compared to baseline for 1h | Fallback to cheaper quantized variant if available |
| downstream_error_rate | downstream.service.errors | any increase above baseline by 2x | Might indicate interface drift; pause rollout |

Automated rollback rules (default):
- If any High-priority SLI breaches during a stage, rollback to previous stable version immediately. High priority = request_error_rate, quality_regression.
- If Latency P99 or P95 crosses thresholds during canary, pause and extend observation window by 60m; if persists, rollback.
- Cost spikes trigger a throttled rollback path: if cost_per_token > 40% and sustained for 60m, lower routing weight to a cost-optimized variant and alert.
- If automatic_rollback is disabled in rollout policy, the system MUST create a page in the incidents queue and notify the rollback authority.

Manual rollback checklist (for rollback authority):
1) Confirm alert and validate against correlated telemetry (traces, logs, eval results).
2) Communicate: post a short status in #incidents and update rollback ticket.
3) Execute rollback via redwoodctl or console:
   redwoodctl rollout rollback --id rlb-2026-029 --to-stable-version v2026-03-01
4) Run quick smoke tests and synthetic load for 10–30 minutes.
5) Post-rollback analysis: fill template in the rollout audit (cause, root-cause hypothesis, mitigation).

Compatibility and contract checks (must-pass):
- API surface: no removed fields without explicit client gating. Backwards-compatible additive changes allowed.
- Tokenization parity: token counts must be within +/-10% for equivalent inputs unless accompanied by change notes.
- Streaming semantics: streaming boundary markers and chunking must match contract; clients expect partial object framing.
- Determinism: for deterministic endpoints, seed/PRNG behavior must be preserved or documented.

Sample contract-verify output (expected):
{
  "result": "PASS",
  "checks": ["schema-match","required-keys","streaming-framing"]
}

Observability runbook (what to look at during a stage):
- Dashboards: canary-summary, p95/p99 latency heatmap, error-kinds pie chart, top-10 callers.
- Traces: sample slow requests and tail traces; look for kernel fallback, OOMs, retry storms.
- Logs: search for serialization errors, tokenizer exceptions, and schema mismatch warnings.
- Eval results: sampled user queries compared against baseline; spot anomalous output patterns.

Ownership, roles and responsibilities:
- Rollout owner: coordinates the rollout, monitors, and owns the rollout metadata.
- Rollback authority: on-call SRE or runtime lead empowered to execute rollback.
- Observability owner: ensures dashboards and alerting exist for the rollout.
- Quality owner: owns eval-harness configuration and quality thresholds.

Audit and postmortem requirements:
- Every non-trivial rollout (any stage >= 25%) requires a short audit entry that includes: rollout id, owner, timestamps of stage transitions, detected signals, and final outcome.
- If rollback occurs, a postmortem is required within 3 business days describing root cause and corrective actions.

Appendix: Common failure modes and mitigations (short):
- Kernel fallback causing p99 spike -> mitigate by prewarming kernels, review compilation flags, or reduce sequence length.
- Tokenizer drift -> freeze tokenizer in artifact and run token-parity tests.
- Sudden cost increase -> route to quantized variant and open cost review.
- Downstream schema mismatch -> add schema adaptor and stop rollout until adapter is deployed.

This playbook is intended to be a living document. Updates to thresholds, SLI names, and CLI commands must be recorded in the rollout metadata and reviewed quarterly by Observability and Runtime teams.
